On this page

Errors ​

Every error skapi-swift throws is a SkapiError with three fields:

  • code: a short name you can check in code, such as INVALID_PARAMETER.
  • message: what went wrong, in plain words.
  • cause: the underlying error or the server's error body, when there is one.
swift
import Skapi

let skapi = try Skapi(projectId: "<Project ID>")

do {
    try await skapi.login(email: "user@example.com", password: "wrong password")
} catch let err as SkapiError {
    print(err.code)     // INCORRECT_USERNAME_OR_PASSWORD
    print(err.message)  // Incorrect username or password.
}

SkapiError is a LocalizedError, so err.localizedDescription reads "<code>: <message>", ready for an alert while you build.

The codes are the same ones skapi-js and skapi-py use, so a check written for one works for the others.

Common codes ​

codemeaning
INVALID_PARAMETERA value you passed is missing, the wrong type, or out of range. The message names it. Nothing was sent.
INVALID_REQUESTThe call is not allowed in this state, for example User login is required.
NOT_EXISTSThe record, file, account or project does not exist.
EXISTSIt already exists, for example an account with that e-mail.
INCORRECT_USERNAME_OR_PASSWORDWrong e-mail, username or password.
MFA_REQUIREDThe password was right and the account has two-step login on: call verifyMFA(code:) with the code. See Two-Step Login.
INVALID_CODEWrong authenticator code. Try the next one.
SIGNUP_CONFIRMATION_NEEDEDThe user has not confirmed their signup yet.
USER_IS_DISABLEDThe account is disabled. See User Profile.
REQUIRE_LOGINThe project only lets signed-in users read its database.
REQUEST_EXCEEDToo many attempts. Wait and try again.
TOO_MANY_REQUESTSThe server kept answering "too many requests" after 6 automatic retries.
NETWORK_ERRORNo answer came back. The user stays signed in; try again when the network is back.
ERRORAnything else. The message says what happened.

Encryption adds its own codes, such as ENCRYPTION_LOCKED; they are listed in the Encryption reference.

Retries ​

skapi-swift retries on its own when the server asks it to slow down (it waits as long as the server says, up to 6 times), and when a token refresh fails (for about 6 seconds). Other errors are thrown at once. A token refresh that still fails for lack of network keeps the session: the call throws NETWORK_ERROR, and the next call after the network is back refreshes again.

Cancelling ​

skapi-swift calls are ordinary async calls. Waiting calls that sleep between checks, such as forwardRequestPoll, stop with Swift's CancellationError when the task that runs them is cancelled, for example when a SwiftUI view's .task ends.
